# Study a Topic with AI

**Languages:** [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README_zh.md)

Turn a short source into explanations, checked practice and a review plan with AI.

[Start this course on AILesson](https://ailesson.io/courses/study-a-topic-with-ai)

An AI explanation can feel clear while it is on screen. The harder moment comes when you close it and try to explain the idea yourself. This course helps you turn a short piece of reading into something you can study, attempt and check.

You will work with a small set of prepared photography notes. The subject stays deliberately narrow: two camera controls and the limits of what those notes can tell you. You need no camera or photography experience. The work is learning how to ask AI for help at your level, check the practice it generates and use an answer to decide what to do next.

The four lessons follow one study session into its next two reviews. You will choose a checkable goal, inspect an explanation, check a question set against the source, examine feedback on clearly supplied sample answers and adapt a short review plan. AI helps organize and respond; you keep the source, make an attempt and decide whether its feedback is supported.

You finish with a compact study method and an example review record that you can adapt to another short source. Completing the course is not a measurement of your photography knowledge or future retention. The useful next step is to try the method with your own material and save what you actually answered.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a camera or photography knowledge?

No. The few subject facts you need are included in the course. You will judge how AI handles those facts, rather than choose settings for a real photograph.

### Do I need a separate AI account?

The course contains the recorded messages and replies needed for the exercises. To repeat the method yourself, use an AI assistant that accepts text; no special study tool or file upload is required.

### Can I use my own notes instead?

Yes. Start with a short source you can check, and remove information you should not share. If the material is incomplete or you cannot verify an answer, keep that question open until you have a suitable source or a knowledgeable person to check it.
